Compared to cohort 1, in which 40% of the patients never received professional tooth cleaning, only a minority (i.e. 9%) of patients in cohort 2 never received a professional tooth cleaning. Furthermore, patients in cohort 2 showed improved oral hygiene attitudes, i.e. they were brushing on average about I min longer compared to patients in cohort 1, and the vast majority (i.e. 77%) _ Springer were using any interdental cleaning device vs. only 40% of the patients in cohort I. In this context, although there was no difference between the cohorts regarding the number of remaining teeth, the improved periodontal status observed in cohort 2 may be due to a more stringent, including timely. extraction policy of severely affected teeth prior to initiation of cancer treatment, compared to cohort 1.
